Raising her peak sales estimate for the drug to $400M, assuming 35% - 40% U.S. market share and no market share from Europe, the analyst argued that $28.5M in Yartemlea sales the company recorded for Q2 “was a huge number.”
Despite more than a 90% rally in Omeros

shares over the past six months, the analyst says that the stock is pricing in no more than $350M in peak sales for the drug. “So even after the move in the stock, we don't think investors are fully giving Yartemlea credit for what this launch could become,” Saunders wrote.
